Test where groups of sequences differ, context by context

Source: R/compare_groups.R
compare_groups.Rd

compare_groups() tests where groups of sequences, such as high and low achievers or two phases of a course, differ, context by context and for the trees as a whole. Groups can differ in two distinct ways: they can reach the same history and then continue differently (a behavioral difference), or they can reach some histories more often than others do (a usage difference). Both are tested for every context represented in the groups' trees and for the trees as a whole, so that a difference can be located in specific pathways rather than reported as one number.

The behavioral difference at a context is the Jensen-Shannon divergence (Lin, 1991), in bits, between the groups' next-state distributions, each group weighted by its count at that context. The usage difference is a \(G^2\) homogeneity statistic on the context's prevalence: its count against the other windows of the same length in each group. The omnibus statistics are the count-weighted sum of the divergences and the sum of the \(G^2\) values. All p-values come from one label permutation: sequences are pooled, group labels are shuffled with group sizes fixed, and every statistic is recomputed from raw counts. Per-context p-values are adjusted for false discovery rate with the Benjamini-Hochberg (1995) procedure, separately for each axis. When one person contributes several sequences, a block identifier restricts the shuffle to within persons, so the null distribution respects that nesting. The result is a transitiontrees_group_comparison object whose tables are read with as.data.frame(); summary() gives a one-row overview and plot() the largest behavioral differences.

compare_groups() handles two or more groups. For one overall distance between two trees with a permutation test, use compare_trees(); it measures the symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence, not the Jensen-Shannon divergence used here. plot_difference() maps the per-context differences of two groups next state by next state.

Usage

compare_groups(group, iter = 999L, min_count = 1L, seed = 1L, block = NULL)

Arguments

group

A transitiontrees_group of unweighted trees, from context_tree(..., group = ).

iter

Number of label permutations. Default 999.

min_count

Contexts with a total count across groups below this are dropped from the table. Default 1.

seed

Seed for the permutations, or NULL to use the current random-number state. Default 1. A non-NULL seed sets the session's random-number state.

block

Block identifiers for a stratified permutation, one per sequence in group-then-row order. Default NULL: the block stored by context_tree(..., block = ) is used when present, and labels are shuffled freely otherwise.

Value

An object of class transitiontrees_group_comparison. Its tables are returned by as.data.frame(): what = "pathways" gives one row per tested context with columns pathway, depth, count_total, one count_<group> and one modal_<group> column per group (the most likely next state), flips (whether the groups' modal next states differ), jsd_bits, jsd_p, jsd_padj, usage_g2, usage_p and usage_padj (NA for the root, which has no usage test), sorted by jsd_bits; what = "omnibus" gives one row per axis; and what = "distance" gives one row per pair of groups with their tree_distance(). summary() returns a one-row overview and plot() the largest behavioral differences.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) group is not a transitiontrees_group, has fewer than two groups, or block does not have one entry per sequence.

transitiontrees_weighted_unsupported

(error) a member tree was fitted with weights; the permutation recounts the raw sequences and would drop them.

transitiontrees_degenerate_permutation

(warning) no block contains more than one group, so the stratified shuffle cannot move any label.

References

Lin, J. (1991). Divergence measures based on the Shannon entropy. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 37(1), 145-151. doi:10.1109/18.61115

Benjamini, Y., & Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: A practical and powerful approach to multiple testing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 57(1), 289-300. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x

See also

summary.transitiontrees_group_comparison, as.data.frame.transitiontrees_group_comparison and plot.transitiontrees_group_comparison for the result; compare_trees() for the pairwise test; plot_difference() for the next-state difference map.

Examples

grp <- context_tree(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", time = "Time",
                    action = "Action", group = "Achiever", max_depth = 1)
cmp <- compare_groups(grp, iter = 20)
cmp
